schemeScope: Combined Ordinary scheme. PDF 1–2 cover and note; 3 general marking note; 4 listening tariffs (and the only print of the 0–6 language deduction); 5–7 transcript (never shown to students); 8–10 listening answers in the paper's order, the Fógra a hAon grid first (PDF 8), ending with the mark-total boxes on PDF 10; 11 composition marking (tariffs, the (i) Cumas Gaeilge / (ii) Beachtas definitions and their 40% : 60% ratio, the bracketed content note, the examiner's Nóta). The 2015 scheme prints no 40-mark table; 21 modified marking (SMM, naming the composition's 40-mark Cumas Gaeilge assessment, with no bands). PDF 12–21 are Paper 2 (its last Nóta tops PDF 21); 22–24 are blank.
reviewMethod: Every paper page (the 2015 Paper 1 is an 8-page question booklet; page 8 is blank) and every applicable scheme page read in the text layer and checked against the printed page (PDF 8, 9, 10 and 11 rendered and compared line by line); each listening prompt and scheme slice is asserted against the PDFs by the builder.

nonPoolDecisions: Listening answers with alternatives (e.g. Dún na nGall / Tír Chonaill; (€)240 / Dhá chéad daichead (euro)) are accepted answers to one task, not routes.

Card unit for listening: six segment cards, because the Bank plays one recording section as one exercise; every printed question is a separate 3-mark criterion (20 questions; the four Fógra a hAon grid questions included; 60 marks). Separate question cards are not added: they would repeat the same prompts inside that exercise.

Composition: closed choose-two of four sections; each printed title is a 50-mark card. Choice is not a route: no two-section combination cards are published; the choose-two instruction is in each title card’s task requirements. Letter/email and dó/di wording stay inside one response.
The modified marking scheme changes assessment for eligible candidates, not the printed tasks.
sourceFindings: Paper 1 = 160: listening 60 (Cuid A 24 = Fógra 1 12 + Fógra 2 12; Cuid B 24 = Comhrá 1 12 + Comhrá 2 12; Cuid C 12 = Píosa 1 6 + Píosa 2 6; every question 3 marks, “3 mharc × 4” / “3 mharc × 2” on PDF 4) and composition 100 (any two of A–D at 50: Tasc 2, Ábhar 8, Cumas Gaeilge 40).
Listening language: “Bainfear ó 0 go 6 ar chaighdeán na Gaeilge” is printed only on scheme PDF 4 in 2015; it is one section-level deduction, and cards state it without applying it.

Fógra a hAon is a printed grid (“Líon isteach an t-eolas atá á lorg sa ghreille anseo.”) of four unnumbered questions; the 2015 scheme prints their answers first (PDF 8), each as “answer 3 mharc” in the grid's right column, with partial prices (“Ó na cairteacha 2 mharc”; “Ticéid 2 mharc chuig ceolchoirmeacha 1 mharc”). Each grid question is its own criterion (labelled Greille 1–4 in the app).

Comhrá a hAon An Dara Mír 2 prints its half-answer rule as text after the answer: “Leictreachas agus teas = 3 mharc Ceann amháin den dá rud (leictreachas nó teas) i gceart, bronn 2 mharc air”; the criterion allows 0, 2 and 3.

The 2015 composition marking prints no headed Tasc, Ábhar and Cumas Gaeilge sections and no 40-mark table: the tariff block (Tasc 2, Ábhar 8, Cumas Gaeilge 40) is the Tasc criterion's text; the bracketed note “[Ní mór ceangal cinnte a bheith idir … nach bhfuil ad rem.]” (no “leanúnach”, which the paper's Treoracha print) is the content guidance, lifted as the Ábhar criterion's text; the (i) Cumas Gaeilge and (ii) Beachtas definitions (“[(i) agus (ii) sa chóimheas 40% : 60%]”) and the examiner's Nóta go with Cumas Gaeilge. The modified-marking page (PDF 21) prints no 40-mark bands.
Paper prints “t-” with ASCII hyphens and “D’fhéach”, “m’fhón” with U+2019; B(i) ends on “…” and B(ii) on “...”; cards keep the paper's characters.
No 2015 Ordinary card existed before this review; the 15 cards are new.
